data.narrative:
Osaro is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Derik Pridmore and Michael Kahane that has raised $86.8M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), with three same-sector, same-stage private companies directly informing the peer-median method.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach anchored on total capital raised ($87M proxy) and applied a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $165M. The peer-median method examined three directly comparable robotics firms at Series B stage—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—producing a median valuation of $1.8B and a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The wide divergence between these methods reflects material uncertainty around whether Osaro's specific traction and defensibility align with the higher-quartile valuations now prevalent in downstream robotics.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $140M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $957M. Stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge substantially, suggesting valuation outcome depends critically on resolution of execution risk and whether Osaro's commercial adoption trajectory tracks peers commanding nine-figure premiums. Further diligence on customer concentration, retention, and path to positive unit economics would materially refine this range.
